notes: Repaired per review: the selector is now a single conjunctive path teams→user_teams→users→channel_members→channels, so the on-call/incident topic filter is applied to the SAME channel row reached via the qualifying Robert's channel_members.channel_id — enforcing that the Robert-named workspace member's own conversation membership is in the on-call channel, not merely that the workspace independently contains some on-call channel elsewhere. This yields T01WORKSPACE ('Test Workspace', via Robert Walsh and/or Robert Chen both members of core-infra, topic mentioning on-call/incidents) and T02VELOCITY ('Velocity Labs', via Robert Kim member of ops-oncall, topic 'On-call rotation and incident triage') as the two genuine matches, consistent with the declared underspecified resolution_mode. T03GAMMA is excluded because Robert Diaz's only channel membership (team-social) has no on-call/incident topic. T04DELTA is excluded because the incident-channel member is Roberta Nguyen, whose display_name 'Roberta' fails the exact-match 'Robert' filter (avoiding the substring-match trap where 'Robert' ⊂ 'Roberta'). Robert Fields (T01WORKSPACE) authors a message in the on-call channel but has no channel_members row there, so he is not picked up by the join and does not spuriously create or reinforce a match, confirming message authorship cannot substitute for CONVERSATION_MEMBERSHIP. The acting user holds workspace membership in all four candidate/negative workspaces (Test Workspace, Velocity Labs, Gamma Corp, Delta Systems) enabling discovery via users.list/conversations.list/conversations.members/conversations.info per the documented access plan.
